The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was set up in Bangkok in August 1967 by five states: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.

The five had just come out of quarrels with each other, above all Indonesia's armed "Confrontation" with the new Malaysia. The Vietnam War was raging next door, and all five feared communist revolt at home. ASEAN gave them a club where they could talk instead of fight, and a common voice toward the big powers of the Cold War.

It works by consensus and does not interfere in members' internal affairs. That makes it slow, but it has kept the peace among its members for decades.

  • Brunei joined in 1984.
  • Vietnam joined in 1995, Laos and Myanmar in 1997, Cambodia in 1999.
  • Timor-Leste became the eleventh member in 2025.

From the 1990s ASEAN turned more to trade, with the ASEAN Free Trade Area and later deals with China, Japan, Korea, India and Australia.
sum: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was set up in Bangkok in August 1967 by five states: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
